item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late August 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026
  • Microsoft internal deployment (MSIT): Available now

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [planForChange] Deprecation of Citrix mVPN Support in Microsoft Edge for Android
item.description:
If your organization does not use Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN) integration support in Microsoft Edge for Android, you can safely disregard this message.

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is retiring Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN) integration support in Microsoft Edge for Android, beginning with Edge version 153. Citrix mVPN integration in Edge for Android depends on legacy third-party components that present ongoing compatibility and maintenance challenges as Android platform requirements continue to evolve.

To help ensure a secure, reliable, and supportable experience for Microsoft Edge users, Microsoft will retire Citrix mVPN integration support in Edge for Android.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Retirement begins in mid-September 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations that currently use Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN) integration with Microsoft Edge for Android.
  • Users who rely on Citrix mVPN to access internal corporate resources through Microsoft Edge for Android.
  • Admins responsible for mobile access, Android device support, or Edge for Android configuration.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Edge for Android
  • Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN)
  • Android devices

What will happen:

  • Microsoft Edge for Android will no longer integrate with Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN).
  • Users who rely on Citrix mVPN to access internal corporate resources through Edge for Android may need to migrate to an alternative supported mobile access solution.
  • Existing workflows that depend specifically on Citrix mVPN integration in Edge for Android may no longer function as expected.
  • This change affects only Citrix mVPN integration and does not impact other Microsoft Edge for Android capabilities.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Administrators should take the following actions:

  • Identify affected users: Determine whether your organization currently uses Citrix Mobile VPN (mVPN) with Microsoft Edge for Android.
  • Review dependencies: Assess business workflows, applications, and internal sites that depend on Citrix mVPN integration in Edge for Android.
  • Plan a migration strategy: Evaluate and validate alternative supported mobile access solutions that meet your organization's requirements.
  • Communicate with impacted users: Inform users of the upcoming change and provide guidance on approved replacement solutions.
  • Complete migration before retirement: Ensure affected users transition away from Citrix mVPN-dependent workflows before support is removed.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] SharePoint: Improved site metadata size reporting
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is improving how site metadata size is reported in SharePoint. The calculation will include document library field data, giving admins a more complete view of a site’s metadata usage.

Nothing about your content changes. No content is added, moved, or removed, and the site metadata size limit remains 1 TB per site.

Because the calculation is more complete, reported metadata size may be higher for some sites. For most sites, the difference will be small and nothing else will change. Some sites may show a size at or above the 1 TB limit once the updated calculation is applied.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on October 20, 2026.
  • Sites already identified as expected to reach or exceed the 1 TB metadata limit will be excluded from the initial rollout to provide additional time to reduce their metadata usage before the correction is applied.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • SharePoint admins who monitor site storage and metadata usage.
  • Organizations with SharePoint sites that are close to or above the 1 TB site metadata limit.
  • Site owners and users of sites that receive metadata warnings or enforcement messages.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint Online.
  • SharePoint Storage Metrics.
  • SharePoint document libraries and lists.

What will happen:

  • Most organizations will see no change in behavior.
  • The visible difference is that reported site metadata size may be higher than before because document library field data is included in the calculation.
  • For sites that cross the 1 TB metadata limit after the correction, the site is blocked from adding new metadata until usage is brought back under the limit.
  • Existing content stays in place and remains accessible.
  • SharePoint shows a warning or error message when the site is close to, or has reached, the metadata limit.
  • For sites that reach 80% of the metadata limit, admins can review the metadata size breakdown on the Storage Metrics page.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is needed for most organizations.

If you see a metadata warning for a site, review its metadata usage and take steps to reduce it:

  • Check the Storage Metrics page for the site. For sites at or above 80% of the metadata limit, the metadata size breakdown is available on this page.
  • Delete unneeded items from your lists and document libraries.
  • Delete older file versions in your document libraries.
  • Remove duplicate files across lists and libraries.
  • Follow the steps provided in the in-product warning message.
  • Re-check the Storage Metrics page after making changes.

If a site remains over the 1 TB metadata limit after the correction is applied, the site will be blocked from adding new metadata until usage is reduced below the limit. Existing content will remain accessible.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. SharePoint metadata size reporting will include document library field data, giving admins a more complete view of site metadata usage. Content is not added, moved, or removed.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. Sites that exceed the 1 TB metadata limit can be blocked from adding new metadata until usage is reduced below the limit, which may affect creation or update actions that add metadata.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Admins will see a more complete metadata size calculation on the Storage Metrics page and may see warning or error messages when a site is close to or over the limit.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows: Organization skill support
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows will support organization skills that admins can upload and share across their tenant. This replaces the earlier “tenant-wide shareable skills” wording with Organization skill support for Copilot in PowerPoint.

This update helps organizations scale approved Copilot skills in PowerPoint with centralized admin management, supporting a more consistent and governed Copilot experience for users.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in early September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Microsoft 365 admins who manage Copilot experiences and organization skills.
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows.
  • Users who access organization-provided Copilot skills in PowerPoint.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot.
  • PowerPoint for Windows.
  • Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Admins will be able to upload organization skills in the Microsoft 365 admin center using the appropriate schema.
  • Admins can share approved organization skills so they appear in Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows.
  • Users can access organization-provided Copilot skills within PowerPoint when those skills are made available by admins.
  • This feature supports centralized governance and distribution of Copilot skills across the organization.
  • The related support article for organization skill support in Copilot in PowerPoint is being prepared by the feature team.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • No action is required before rollout unless your organization plans to publish organization skills for PowerPoint.
  • Review your organization’s governance process for Copilot skills.
  • Identify which organization skills should be shared broadly across your tenant.
  • Prepare admins who manage Microsoft 365 Copilot to upload skills in the Microsoft 365 admin center using the required schema.
  • Update internal Copilot or PowerPoint guidance if your organization documents how users access approved organization skills.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Organization skills can extend Copilot in PowerPoint experiences that interact with user prompts and organizational data available to Copilot.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can access organization-provided Copilot skills in PowerPoint when admins make those skills available.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Admins can centrally manage and distribute organization skills through the Microsoft 365 admin center, supporting governance of available Copilot skills.
Does the change include an admin control and, can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can upload and manage organization skills in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The request does not state whether this can be scoped through Entra ID group membership.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 profile card: View dotted-line managers in the organization panel
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing an additive user interface update to the organization panel in the Microsoft 365 profile card that can display a person's dotted-line manager relationship, in addition to their direct manager, when that data is available. This update helps employees better understand organizational structures in companies where reporting relationships span projects, business units, regions, or functions.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in organizations that provide dotted-line manager relationship data.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 profile card

What will happen

  • Users may see an additional manager relationship in the organization panel representing a dotted-line manager. Organizations may use different labels for this relationship, such as People Lead or Capability Manager.
  • Users can open the dotted-line manager's profile directly from the profile card to learn more about that person's role and organizational context.
  • This is an additive update to the user interface. If dotted-line manager data is not available, no additional manager relationship will be shown.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. If your organization wants dotted-line manager relationships to appear in the Microsoft 365 profile card:

  • Ensure dotted-line manager attributes exist in your HR system and are available for ingestion.
  • Confirm your HR integration is configured through supported organizational data integrations, such as SAP SuccessFactors or Workday.
  • Review internal help desk guidance and documentation so support teams understand why users may see an additional manager relationship label in the organization panel. The displayed relationship name depends on your HR system's role labels.

[Learn more]

  • Overview of people relationships in Microsoft 365 - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn
  • Use your organizational data in Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Viva - Microsoft 365 Apps | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Final reminder: Microsoft Project Online retires on September 30, 2026
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft Project Online will retire on September 30, 2026.  

If users are still using Project Online, they will see an in-app banner announcing the retirement. 

If your organization will not be fully migrated by September 30, 2026, we highly recommend you contact a Microsoft partner immediately to make a migration plan and let your Microsoft account team know your plans.  

At Microsoft, we are committed to empowering every organization with a unified, AI-powered and collaborative work management experience that brings together tasks, plans, and projects in one seamless platform. As part of this commitment, we announced the retirement of Project Online last September. The decision reflects our focus on delivering solutions that are modern, scalable, and future-ready—enabling organizations to benefit from the latest innovations in AI, automation, and collaboration.  Moving to our next-generation platforms brings enhanced productivity, deeper integration with Microsoft 365, and new capabilities designed for the way people work today and tomorrow. 

This update is exclusive to Project Online and does not affect Project desktop/Project Online desktop, Project Server, or Planner.  

We recognize that every organization is unique, with different project management needs and technical requirements. To ensure a smooth transition and continued success, Microsoft is providing three clear paths forward. 

  1. Microsoft Planner: For organizations seeking a modern, cloud-first, and AI-powered project management experience, Planner is designed for flexibility, collaboration, and scalability—empowering teams to manage everything from simple tasks to complex projects in one unified platform. The premium features of Planner included in our Planner and Project Plan 3 license, offer advanced features such as portfolios, baselines, dependencies, and Gantt charts. 
  2. Project Server Subscription Edition: For organizations with advanced project and portfolio management (PPM) requirements, or those needing a short-term solution before moving to the cloud, Project Server Subscription Edition offers comprehensive tools for planning, scheduling, and resource management—built on the latest SharePoint Server technology. 
  3. Project Operations: For Dynamics ERP customers, especially those focused on timesheets and resource scheduling. 

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD:  September 30, 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • After Project Online is retired, you will no longer be able to access your projects or any associated data within the service.  
  • To avoid disruption and potential data loss, it's essential that you complete your transition to any of the alternatives before the retirement date. 
  • You can get details about your organization's Project Online usage by following the Export user data from Project Online documentation.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Identify a Microsoft Partner immediately to help you move off Project Online by month end. To find a partner, contact your Microsoft Sales Representative for a list of recommended partners in your region. 
  • Evaluate the alternatives proposed above and plan the transition immediately. 
  • Migrate your data, if needed, before the retirement date. 
  • This retirement will happen automatically on the specified dates with no admin action required. 
  • You may want to notify your users and update any internal documentation to reflect the above changes. 
  • Review documentation to learn more about how to Prepare for Project Online retirement.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Apps: Cloud Update - Extended rollback support for Monthly Enterprise Channel
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Cloud Update is expanding rollback options for devices on Monthly Enterprise Channel. Administrators will be able to roll back devices to a release from two versions prior, with the latest available security updates for that release, and keep devices in the rolled-back state across subsequent releases until they are ready to resume updates. This provides additional time to investigate and resolve compatibility issues while maintaining security coverage and centralized control through the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This feature gives administrators an additional recovery option for Monthly Enterprise Channel devices managed by Cloud Update. If an update causes a compatibility or operational issue, administrators can roll back affected devices to a release from two versions prior, with the latest available security updates for that release. Devices can remain on the selected version across subsequent releases until the administrator chooses to resume updates. Existing update profiles and devices will not be changed or rolled back automatically.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout. The additional rollback option will become available automatically in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Administrators should review their rollback and recovery procedures, identify who is authorized to initiate a rollback, and update internal support documentation as needed. Before using the feature, assess the affected devices or groups and establish a plan to resume updates after the underlying issue is resolved.

[Compliance considerations:]

The feature includes or affects admin controls, policies, permissions, roles, authentication, or management settings as described in this message. Review the linked documentation or admin center controls for group-based configuration support.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams Rooms: Identify in-room participants with IntelliFrame people labels
item.description:
Updated September 24, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

We're introducing IntelliFrame people labels in Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows to improve meeting clarity and inclusivity for remote participants. When enabled, this feature identifies in-room participants by name and displays a contact card, helping remote attendees easily recognize speakers and follow conversations.

This enhancement supports better hybrid meeting experiences by connecting in-room and remote participants more effectively, improving collaboration and productivity.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566700.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October) expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with Teams Rooms Pro licenses
  • In-room participants who have enrolled in voice and face recognition (People Recognition)

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams Rooms on Windows devices
  • Supported intelligent camera hardware

What will happen:

  • IntelliFrame will display name labels under identified in-room participants’ video feeds.
  • Remote participants can select a label to view a contact card with organizational details.
  • The feature is enabled automatically when prerequisites are met.
  • Existing Teams meeting policies for voice and face enrollment are honored.
  • Participants without enrolled profiles will appear without labels.
  • No change occurs if voice and face enrollment is disabled in your organization.

Screenshot - IntelliFrame people labels identify enrolled in-room participants by name, helping remote attendees recognize who's speaking; selecting a label opens the person's contact card

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required to enable this feature.

To maximize value, administrators may:

  • Review and confirm Teams Rooms devices:
    • Ensure devices are licensed with Teams Rooms Pro.
    • Verify use of supported intelligent cameras.
  • Review and update meeting policies:
    • Allow enrollment: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Enabled.
    • Enable name display in rooms: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride On.
  • Encourage users to enroll in voice and face recognition: Teams > Settings > Recognition.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance.
  • Notify users about this capability to drive awareness and adoption.

To disable IntelliFrame people labels, administrators can:

  • Turn off in-room name display (labels stop; other IntelliFrame framing unaffected): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride Off
  • Block voice and face enrollment entirely (no one can be identified by name): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Disabled
  • Individual users can opt out anytime by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.

Learn more: 

  • What is Microsoft Multi-Stream IntelliFrame and Intelligent Camera? | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Enable People Recognition on Teams Rooms (voice & face policies) | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Overview and configuration of voice and face enrollment | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance AreaImpact
Introduces or modifies AI/ML capabilitiesUses AI-based biometric identification (voice and face profiles) to identify in-room participants. Identification occurs only for users who have consented and completed People Recognition enrollment.
Stores new customer dataThis feature does not create new data; it relies on existing voice and face profiles from People Recognition enrollment, governed by the organization’s current configuration.
Alters processing of existing customer dataParticipant identity data is processed differently when recognition is enabled.
Provides new way of communicating between usersLabels and contact cards enhance visibility of in-room participants for remote users.
Adds or changes admin controlsControlled via Teams meeting policies (EnrollUserOverride and RoomPeopleNameUserOverride).
Allows users to enable/disable the featureUsers can enroll or opt out of voice and face profiles in Teams settings.

item.title: [stayInformed] Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID
item.description:
On August 24, 2026, we initiated the gradual roll out of self-service migrations to Microsoft Entra Agent IDs for Copilot Studio agents in Power Platform Advisor. Beginning on September 2026, automatic migrations of agents without Entra Agent ID to Microsoft Entra Agent ID were also initiated. Copilot Studio agents created before May 2026 may still use legacy app-registration identities. We recommend migrating any of your remaining agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID.

How does this affect me?
Migrating your agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID helps your organization build, discover, govern, and protect agent identities across services by using a unified platform.

Key benefits include:
  • Audit logging in Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Agent lifecycle management.
  • Integration with Entra ID Governance.
  • Visibility of connector permissions as API permissions on the agent identity, so Entra and Microsoft 365 admins can see what an agent can do without opening Power Platform admin center.
  • Ability to target those connector permissions with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies (for example, network location, device compliance, or risk conditions).
To find out if your agent has been migrated already been migrated or if there are any agents that remain to be migrated in your tenant, you can use the Advisor recommendation.

What action do I need to take?
We recommend identifying and migrating your eligible agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID. To perform this mitigation, please follow the steps listed below:
  1. Confirm that Power Platform inventory is enabled for your tenant.
  2. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Actions > Recommendations > Active, and open Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID for enhanced agent governance.
  3. In the recommendation pane, expand Why is this important?, and review the migration guidance.
  4. Review the eligible agents. Use Suggested migration order and Migration notes to choose an initial pilot or the next migration batch. The table also provides information such as environment, environment type, owner, recent activity, and authentication method.
  5. Select the checkbox next to each agent you want to migrate. You can select one agent or multiple eligible agents. The Migrate button becomes available and the action bar shows the number of agents selected.
  6. Select Migrate, review the confirmation, and confirm the migration. Start with a small batch of noncritical agents.
  7. Review the Action, Action state, and Action date columns for each selected agent. To review actions across recommendations, select the Action history tab.
  8. Coordinate a validation window with the makers who own the agents.
  9. After migration, validate each agent's channels, authentication, actions, connectors, flows, and integrations before migrating another batch.
  10. Review Microsoft Entra sign-in logs and applicable Conditional Access results. If an agent does not pass validation, revert it before continuing.
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

For more information, please visit Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: AI-powered notes for in-person meetings with Facilitator in Teams Rooms on Android
item.description:
Updated September 24, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

To support more effective in-person collaboration, Microsoft Teams is expanding AI-powered meeting notes with the Facilitator agent to Teams Rooms on Android. This enhancement allows teams meeting in a physical room to capture real-time notes, decisions, and action items—without requiring a scheduled or hybrid meeting. The experience is designed to ensure notes are securely stored in your tenant while no data remains on the room device after the meeting ends.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 56700.

[When this will happen]

General Availability

  • Worldwide and GCC: We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 (previously late October) expect to complete by early December 2026 (previously mid-November).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Teams Rooms on Android
  • Rooms licensed with Teams Rooms Pro

What will happen

  • During an in-person meeting, users can start AI-powered notes by selecting the Take notes button on the Teams Rooms console.
  • Notes appear on the front-of-room display or touch board during the meeting: 
  • Notes are stored in tenant-owned SharePoint embedded storage.
  • Access to notes requires adding your work account using the Access notes button on the Teams Rooms console.
  • After the meeting, notes can be viewed and edited by participants with access via the meeting recap in the meeting chat on the Teams desktop client.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Admins can control profanity filtering in meeting transcripts

This gives organizations a policy-controlled option for workflows in which words that are currently masked need to remain visible in the transcript.

If an administrator turns filtering off for the policy assigned to a meeting organizer, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in both the live and saved transcript for that organizer's scheduled meetings. This change does not add an organizer-level control and does not change each participant's live-caption profanity preference.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments
item.description:
Updated September 23, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

As part of our overall security initiatives, we’ve created a separate internal application configuration for Outlook attachments, therefore, all standard security and authentication flows will be handled separately. Moreover, Conditional Access policies are now enforced for Outlook attachment operations. Users who don’t meet company policies won’t be able to download, preview, or upload classic attachments (this includes inline images). Policies assigned to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be inherited by the attachment application by default. Continuous Access Evaluation is not included in the initial rollout but will follow up soon.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • Your existing policies now cover attachments. Conditional Access policies you have already scoped to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be enforced for attachment scenarios as well. No new policies need to be created.
  • Users out of compliance will be blocked from attachments. If a user's session no longer satisfies a Conditional Access policy — for example, a non-compliant device, a blocked location, or a network change that triggers CAE re-evaluation — attachment operations will be blocked.
  • These are separate follow-up changes we expect to land in the upcoming weeks. We’ll keep you updated on the readiness and rollout of these enhancements:
    • User sign in prompt for remediation. We're currently working on a solution to prompt the user for sign in to recover functionalities when possible. This will depend on the policy configuration; if the user is not compliant, they won’t be able to use attachment-related tasks. We’ll provide an update to customers once we start rolling out this enhancement.
    • Enable Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE). CAE isn’t supported for this new application configuration yet. We’ll update this message with additional content when it becomes available.  

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  1. Review how your Office and Exchange policies apply to attachments.
    1. Attachment operations are now handled by their own application, which by default inherits the Conditional Access policies you've assigned to Office and Exchange. Confirm those conditions are what you intend to enforce for attachments.
    2. If you’ve intentionally excluded Exchange online from a policy, that exclusion doesn't carry over to attachments, so users in scope can reach their mail but will be blocked from downloading, previewing, or uploading attachments.
    3. To manage attachment policies separate from mail, you can either exclude the attachment application from a policy or target it in a policy of its own. Both require a one-time setup step in your tenant — see Appendix: Excluding attachments from a policy.
  2. Update your help desk documentation. Support staff should know that attachment access failures may now result from a Conditional Access policy, and that the remediation is the same as for Outlook — return to a compliant device or network and re-authenticate.
  3. Notify users if you enforce strict Conditional Access policies, so they understand attachment actions may now be blocked under the same conditions that already block access to their mailbox.

[Appendix:]

Excluding attachments from a policy

Attachment operations are handled by an application named OwaDownloadAttachments (application Id: e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64 ). Before you can exclude it from a Conditional Access policy, a service principal for it must exist in your tenant. This is a one-time step you'll need to complete first.

Step 1: Create the service principal

You'll need the Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator role.

  1. Open Graph Explorer and sign in as an administrator of your tenant.
  2. Run:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals

Request body: { "appId": "e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64" }

Consent to Application.ReadWrite.All scope is required.

A successful request returns 201 Created with a display name of OwaDownloadAttachments. If the request reports that the service principal already exists, continue to Step 2.

Step 2: Exclude it from the policy

  1. Click on View or Edit on the Conditional Access Policy you want to update.
  2. Under Target resources, select the Exclude tab.
  3. Choose Select resources, search for OwaDownloadAttachments, and select it.
  4. Save the policy.

Repeat Step 2 for each policy you want attachment operations exempted from.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Default visibility of additional profile card properties in Microsoft 365 profile cards
item.description:
Updated September 22, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

To help people discover and understand organizational information more easily, Microsoft is changing the default visibility of 11 existing profile card properties in Microsoft 365 profile cards. Today, these properties can be populated from Microsoft Entra ID and other supported external data sources such as People Graph Connectors and Microsoft 365 Organizational Data, but they are disabled by default and require administrators to manually enable them. You can find more on the existing profile card property management here.

With this update, these properties will be displayed by default when populated with data. This helps organizations surface relevant employee information more consistently while reducing administrative effort for commonly used profile attributes. Organizations retain administrative controls to manage visibility according to their business, privacy, and compliance requirements.

The following properties are included in this update:

  1. Division
  2. Role
  3. Employee number
  4. Employee type
  5. Cost center
  6. User principal name (UPN)
  7. Alias
  8. Fax
  9. Street address
  10. State
  11. Postal code

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rollout in late October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact to your organization:]

Who is affected

  1. Global Administrators and People Administrators responsible for profile card management.
  2. Organizations with users whose profile data includes one or more of the affected properties.

Platforms/Services

  1. Microsoft 365 Profile Cards
  2. Microsoft Entra ID
  3. Microsoft 365 Organizational Data
  4. Microsoft Entra People Graph Connectors
  5. Microsoft Graph profile card management APIs
  6. Microsoft 365 admin center

What will happen

  1. The 11 listed properties will automatically appear on profile cards when the corresponding attributes contain data.
  2. The change is enabled by default.
  3. Attributes sourced from Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Organizational Data, and Microsoft Entra People Graph Connectors follow the same visibility behavior.
  4. No changes are made to underlying attribute values or source systems.
  5. No changes are required from end users.
  6. Tenants that have never configured profile card settings will automatically receive the new default visibility behavior.
  7. Only properties with populated values will appear on profile cards.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

If your organization does not want specific properties displayed on profile cards, action is recommended before October 31, 2026.

Review current profile card configuration

Use Microsoft Graph to review existing profile card property settings:

HTTP

GET  https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties 

Hide properties before rollout

To prevent a property from being displayed, configure the property as hidden using Microsoft Graph.

Example: Hide Employee Number

HTTP

POST

https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties 

Content-Type: application/json 

{ 

"directoryPropertyName": "EmployeeId", 

 "isVisible": false  

} 

For each property, you can use the property mappings below:

Profile card label directoryPropertyName
Division Division
Role Role
Employee number EmployeeId
Employee type EmployeeType
Cost center CostCenter
User principal name (UPN) UserPrincipalName
Alias Alias
Fax Fax
Street address StreetAddress
State StateOrProvince
Postal code PostalCode

Important: Each property requires a separate Microsoft Graph API call. Bulk enable or bulk disable operations are not currently supported.

You can find more on using Microsoft Graph APIs for showing and hiding profile card attributes here.

Recommended Administrator Actions

  1. Verify your current profile card configuration using Microsoft Graph and review which of the affected properties contain data in your tenant.
  2. Use Microsoft Graph Profile Card APIs to hide any properties that should remain unavailable to users before rollout begins on October 31, 2026.
  3. Communicate the upcoming change to help desk and support teams.

After rollout, administrators can continue managing profile card visibility through Microsoft 365 admin center > People settings > Profile cards. Changes made can take up to 24 hours to be reflected on profile cards across Microsoft 365 experiences.

Customized reports will remain associated with the report version from which they were originally created and will not be automatically migrated to newer report versions.

This approach preserves report integrity and prevents customizations from breaking or behaving unexpectedly when significant report updates are introduced. Users retain access to their existing customized reports while maintaining control over when to adopt newer report versions and capabilities.

[Rollout Schedule:]

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Customized reports will not automatically migrate to newer major report versions.
  • Existing customized reports remain accessible.
  • Older report versions may stop receiving refreshed data.
  • Users may see an "A newer version of this report is available" message.
  • Users who need the latest data and capabilities must create a new customized copy from the latest report version.
  • No admin configuration is required.
  • No policy or tenant setting changes are introduced.

Example: A customized Copilot Adoption report based on an older report version may continue displaying data through July 26, while the latest report displays data through August 8. The customized report remains on the older version and does not automatically receive newer data.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Federated Copilot connectors support create, update, and delete actions
item.description:
[What and why]

Federated Copilot connectors currently allow Microsoft 365 Copilot to retrieve data from third-party services in real time. With this update, supported connector tools that create, update, and delete content in those services will become available in Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences, helping users complete tasks without leaving Copilot. Actions are performed using the signed-in user's account and permissions in the third-party service, and by default each create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs. Administrators can review each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that do not meet their organization's requirements.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that have federated Copilot connectors enabled
  • Users who connect federated Copilot connectors to supported third-party services
  • Administrators who manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Connected third-party services

What will happen

  • Supported connector tools that create, update, or delete content in third-party services will become available in supported Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences.
  • Available actions depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher.
  • Federated Copilot connectors used in Researcher will remain read-only.
  • Users must authenticate to the third-party service before using authenticated connector capabilities.
  • User approval is required before create, update or delete actions
  • Before an action runs, Copilot displays the action and the parameters that will be sent to the third-party service.
  • Users can select Cancel, Allow once, or Always allow for a specific tool.
  • If a connector publisher adds or changes a tool that can create, update, or delete content, that tool returns to a state that requires approval.
  • Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot Settings > Sources.
  • If a user does not approve an action, the action is not performed.
  • Existing federated connector availability controls continue to apply.
  • A new MCP tools section will be available on each federated connector details page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Administrators can review the tools exposed by the connector, including tools that can modify or delete data.

Federated Copilot connectors continue to access external data in real time using the user's identity and permissions. External data is not indexed into Microsoft 365.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to receive this feature.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review enabled federated Copilot connectors to determine which connectors may expose tools that create, update, or delete content.
  • Review connector capabilities against organizational security, compliance, and acceptable-use requirements.
  • Disable connectors that do not meet organizational requirements.
  • Review agreements with third-party providers, including applicable licensing, privacy, data residency, and acceptable-use requirements.
  • Update user and help-desk guidance so users understand that actions are performed using their permissions in the third-party service.
  • Review the updated Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors Terms of use.

Learn more

  • Federated connectors overview - Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors | Microsoft Learn will be updated before release

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Supported federated Copilot connector tools can create, update, and delete content in connected third-party services using the signed-in user's permissions. External data continues to be accessed in real time and is not indexed into Microsoft 365.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. In addition to retrieving information, Microsoft 365 Copilot can invoke supported connector tools that create, update, or delete content in connected third-party services.
Does the change add any integration to third-party software products?Yes. Microsoft 365 Copilot can invoke supported tools exposed by federated Copilot connectors that create, update, or delete content in connected third-party services.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Existing connector availability controls continue to apply, and administrators can review connector tools and disable connectors that do not meet organizational requirements.
Does the change allow users to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can manage approval preferences for connector tools and can review or reset tool permissions through Copilot Settings > Sources.
